beats.say: Noise-cancelling headphones don't just block noise. They fight sound with more sound, and the two cancel each other out.
Sound is a wave in the air. Its peaks push, and its dips pull, and that pattern is what reaches your ear.
Tiny microphones on the outside of each ear cup listen to the noise around you, all the time.
A chip instantly flips that wave upside down. Every peak becomes a dip, and every dip becomes a peak.
The speaker plays that flipped wave right into your ear, at the very same moment, along with your music.
The noise and its opposite meet, and they cancel out. A flat line. All that is left is quiet.
It works best on steady hums, like an engine, because they repeat and are easy to predict.
Sudden sounds, like a voice, change too fast to flip in time, so they still sneak through.
On a plane, the drone fades away, but someone saying your name doesn't.
Follow for how things work, in a minute.
